title: Guest room
topic: A friend is measuring a bigger guest bed against the walkway
blurb: A friend is swapping the guest bed and doing the measurements in the chat.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The swap
segments.text: Putting a 6-foot bed in the guest room to replace the 5-foot one that's in there now.

segments.label: The layout
segments.text: The current bed is pushed along the window wall, leaving a 2-foot walkway on the closet side.

segments.label: The math
segments.text: The new one is a foot wider, so that's half a foot off each side — still a 1.5-foot walkway, plenty of room to open the closet.

segments.label: The order
segments.text: I'll order it tonight before the weekend sale ends.

conclusion: A foot wider means half a foot off each side, so the closet walkway only shrinks to 1.5 feet.

flaws.original: One side is already against the wall, so the whole extra foot comes out of the walkway — that's 1 foot left, not 1.5.
flaws.corrupted: The new one is a foot wider, so that's half a foot off each side — still a 1.5-foot walkway, plenty of room to open the closet.

diagnosis_choices.label: The bed is already against the wall, so the whole extra foot comes out of the walkway — you'll have 1 foot, not 1.5.
A 6-foot bed plus a 2-foot walkway is 8 feet, and the room is only 7, so the bed won't fit at all.
Closet doors need a full 2 feet to open, so even a 1.5-foot walkway would be too tight.

fix_choices.label: Take the whole extra foot from the walkway: 2 feet minus 1 foot leaves 1 foot, not 1.5.
Pull the bed off the wall so the extra width can split on both sides.
Keep the 5-foot bed; a 6-foot bed can never leave a walkway in this room.

flaws.explanation: The bed can't grow through the wall. That whole extra foot comes straight out of your walkway.
flaws.why_tempting: Splitting a width change 'half and half' feels automatic. It's easy to skip that one edge is already tight against a wall.
flaws.catch_rule: If one side of a bed or desk is already against a wall, every extra inch of width comes out of the open side.
flaws.hint: The current bed is already tight against one wall. Where can the extra foot actually go?

practice.problem: A sofa sits along one wall with a 90cm gap to the coffee table. A new sofa is 20cm deeper. A friend says, '10cm off each side, still 80cm to the table.' What's wrong?
practice.answer: The back is already against the wall, so all 20cm come out of the gap. That's 70cm left, not 80.

clean_conclusion: The extra foot all comes out of the walkway. You'll have 1 foot, not 1.5.

diagnosis: Moving from a 5-foot bed to a 6-foot bed makes it narrower.
The new bed adds six feet to the old width.
Replacing the old bed means adding their widths.
fix: Treat the new bed as saving one foot.
Count both beds in the room after replacement.

diagnosis: The 2-foot walkway is split between the sides of the bed.
The wall side is where the closet walkway sits.
The 2-foot figure is the width of the existing bed.
fix: Use one foot of clearance on each side.
Put the walkway between the bed and window wall.
Use two feet as the current bed width.
